clue.text: Argue son needs to get into puzzles

indicators.note: the son must go inside the word for puzzles, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: crosswords are word puzzles

explanation.surface: A parent tells a quarrelsome boy to go and do some puzzles instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs to get into' puts S between CROSS and WORDS, giving the run of three S's.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords is an idiom for having a dispute or quarrel with someone.

clue.text: I'm surprised face is friendly

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Someone is taken aback that a stranger's expression is so warm.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a casual British exclamation, like 'blimey'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial is a synonym for warm and amiable in manner.

clue.text: Musician loves catching prelude from Bach first

indicators.note: the two loves hold the next letter between them, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O; two loves give OO

indicators.note: a prelude comes at the start, so this takes the opening letter of the composer's name

parts.note: 1st, written with I for the numeral one

explanation.surface: A performer adores playing Bach before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts B (the start of Bach) between two O's for OBO; 'first' is written 1ST, the 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist is an orchestral player of the oboe.

clue.text: If you don't succeed, you'll fail — as you may in the pools?

definitions.text: If you don't succeed, you'll fail
definitions.meaning: ... describes a situation where success or failure rests on your own efforts

definitions.text: as you may in the pools?
definitions.meaning: in a swimming pool you literally either ...

explanation.surface: A warning about a do-or-die venture, with a jokey nod to gambling on the football pools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pools' suggests the football pools, a British betting game on match results; here it means swimming pools.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being left to survive or fail with no help, matching an all-or-nothing outcome.

clue.text: Yarn in The Telegraph and another newspaper

parts.note: the newspaper speaking of itself says we
FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A story appears both in this paper and in a rival one.
explanation.walkthrough: A newspaper's editorial voice is 'we', so The Telegraph, printing this clue, is WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Weft is the crosswise thread woven through the warp, a kind of yarn.

clue.text: Can opener call on kind of cricket shot?

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sitting on another comes above it, so first

parts.note: to ring is to telephone
a pull is a cricket stroke hitting a short ball to the leg side

explanation.surface: Can someone who opens the batting phone about a particular stroke?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can opener' looks like a tin opener or a cricket opening batsman; it is the tab on a drinks can.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring pull is the metal tab that opens a drinks can.

clue.text: The compiler's work environment

definitions.meaning: a crossword compiler is called a setter
the surroundings in which something happens

explanation.surface: A setter describes the surroundings in which they produce crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting means both the act of composing a crossword and a surrounding context or backdrop.

clue.text: Favouring Miss Doone, almost without hope

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: the name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel

explanation.surface: A hopeless admirer of the heroine Lorna Doone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' removes the last A of LORNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Forlorn describes someone pitifully sad and lacking any expectation of success.

clue.text: Went wrong when serving cooked tofu with old feta

indicators.note: food that is cooked is altered, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A waiter made a mistake bringing out stale cheese with tofu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving' looks like waiting at table; it is tennis serving.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a server who oversteps the baseline commits a foot fault, an error at service.

clue.text: Overkeen supporter in fact heading for Arsenal ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so these letters are rearranged
the head of the club name is its first letter

explanation.surface: An obsessive football fan is actually on his way to Arsenal's stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a football stadium; it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatic is a zealot, someone with excessive enthusiasm for a cause or team.

clue.text: Legal agreement, one dealing with labour movement?

parts.note: a contract is a legally binding agreement
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A union contract with someone handling the workers' movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'labour movement' suggests trade unions; it is the tightening of the womb in childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Contractions are the muscular spasms of the womb during childbirth labour.

clue.text: Leaving out nothing, given important task

parts.note: zero is written as the letter O
a mission is a vital assignment

explanation.surface: Skipping nothing when handed a significant job.
explanation.definitionFit: Omission is the act of excluding or failing to include something.

clue.text: Choice of work not holding one back

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: back means the word not with its passenger is read from the end
the word not keeps the numeral inside it

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Deciding on a job that doesn't need to restrain anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts I inside NOT for NOIT; 'back' reverses it to TION.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is one of the alternatives available to select.

clue.text: Working out script with old ham from Italy

indicators.note: working dough or clay reshapes it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drafting a script with an elderly hammy Italian actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges OUT and SCRIPT; 'ham' looks like an overacting performer but is cured pork.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosciutto is the Italian dry-cured ham, often served thinly sliced.

clue.text: Chap releasing cry of pain took a tumble

indicators.note: letting go of something means it is taken out of the word

parts.note: a fellow is a man or chap
ow is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A man who stops yelling in pain after he has fallen over.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell is the past tense of fall, so it means toppled over.

clue.text: Speculator in futures has awfully large torso

indicators.note: something done awfully is messed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stock-market trader with a bloated upper body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speculator in futures' suggests a financial trader; it means someone predicting the future.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrologer forecasts what lies ahead by reading the stars, speculating about coming events.

clue.text: Tailor to repeat light work

indicators.note: to tailor something is to alter it to fit, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dressmaker told to redo some easy sewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light work' looks like an easy task; it is a light musical piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short, light-hearted opera, a less weighty musical composition.

clue.text: Most miserable in Spain, het up when travelling

indicators.note: letters that travel move about, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tourist in Spain who is grumpy and agitated while on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhappiest is the superlative of unhappy, the saddest of all.

clue.text: People get suspended receiving this punishment?

definitions.text: People get suspended receiving this punishment?

parts.words: People get suspended receiving this punishment?
parts.note: suspended looks like being barred from school or work; here it means literally dangling from a rope

explanation.surface: Wondering which penalty leads to people being suspended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspended' usually means barred for a time; here it means hung up by the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Execution by the noose leaves the condemned hanging in mid-air, a capital punishment.

clue.text: Great bronze picture frames

indicators.note: the two words surround the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: A bronze-coloured frame around a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic, informally, means tremendous or impressive.

clue.text: Leader about to interrupt Sunak? That is right

indicators.note: the short word for about breaks into the title of Sunak

parts.note: Rishi Sunak was UK Prime Minister, PM
re means concerning
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A heckler is about to cut in on Rishi Sunak, insisting they're correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was British Prime Minister, so PM.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier is another title for a prime minister or head of government.

clue.text: Cases of player even winning in deal made before match

indicators.note: cases are outer shells, so take each word's first and last letters

parts.note: up means ahead, as in a game

explanation.surface: A sports contract fixed before a game, with a player level then ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a sporting fixture; it means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A prenup is a prenuptial agreement signed before a wedding.

clue.text: Singers sounded out notes

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word for notes resembles another word

parts.note: tenners are ten-pound banknotes

explanation.surface: A choir performed some musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' looks musical but means banknotes: a tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenors are male singers with the highest natural adult voice.

clue.text: Detective inspector arresting country's old statesman

indicators.note: the officer holds the country inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Israel is a country

explanation.surface: A police officer detains a nation's former politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of country's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Flag Alexa's competitor raised

indicators.note: in a down answer lifting a word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: Siri is Apple's voice assistant, a rival to Amazon's Alexa

explanation.surface: A voice assistant's rival hoisted a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner; it is the yellow flag, a wild iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is a common name for the iris plant, especially the yellow wetland species.

clue.text: Vagabond's foot less damp on the outside

indicators.note: the comparative sits outside the abbreviation, wrapping it

parts.note: drier is the comparative of dry

explanation.surface: A tramp's foot is less wet on its outer surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vagabond's' is 'Vagabond is', with the 's a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter wanders from place to place with no settled home, like a tramp.

clue.text: Figure boy must admit current stress

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: admitting lets something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a son is a boy
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A lad has to confess the present strain he is under.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is mental or physical strain.

clue.text: Oddly, German's someone buying a little green jumper

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters of the word

parts.note: a shopper buys goods

explanation.surface: Strangely, a German shopper is purchasing a small green sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a British sweater; it is a leaping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A grasshopper is a small green insect that leaps on long hind legs.
